message.content:
Profit Margin = \(\dfrac{\text{Revenue – Expenses}}{\text{Revenue}}\times100\%\)

For your numbers:

* Revenue = \$200,000  
* Expenses = \$150,000  

\( \displaystyle \text{Profit Margin}= \frac{200\,000-150\,000}{200\,000}\times100\%
   = \frac{50\,000}{200\,000}\times100\%
   = 0.25\times100\%
   = 25\%.\)

So the company's profit margin is **25 percent**.
message.reasoning:
The user wants "profit margin" which is typically calculated as (Revenue - Expenses)/Revenue *100%. They gave revenue=200k, expenses=150k. So profit margin = (50k/200k)*100% = 25%.
